clue.text: Is this for kindling an artistic impression?

definitions.text: Is this for kindling an artistic impression?

blocks.note: surface reading: timber chopped up to start a fire
setter's reading: a print taken from a carved wooden block

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether chopped timber for the fire might count as art.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as WOOD CUT, it is firewood; read as one word, it is a print made by inking a carved block.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodcut is a relief print made from an engraved block of timber, so it is an impression in the printmaking sense.

clue.text: Sort of fence, often daubed

blocks.note: a woven fence or hurdle of interlaced sticks
the same woven sticks plastered with mud in the old building method paired with daub

explanation.surface: A garden fence that keeps getting smeared with paint or mud.
explanation.walkthrough: Wattle and daub is the traditional building method of woven sticks plastered with clay, which is why the fence is often daubed.
explanation.definitionFit: Wattle means interwoven rods and twigs, used for hurdles and fencing and as the frame of plastered walls.

clue.text: Beard, giving striking appearance

blocks.note: first meaning: as a verb, to confront someone boldly
second meaning, read cryptically: putting on a face that stands out

explanation.surface: A beard that gives a man a striking look.
explanation.walkthrough: Beard here is the verb, to defy someone to their face, not facial hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To outface someone is to stare them down or defy them boldly, the same sense as bearding a lion in its den.

clue.text: Suit royal household barge, for example

blocks.note: a monarch's court is the royal household
a barge is one kind of vessel

explanation.surface: A list of things belonging to royalty, such as the state barge.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay suit to someone is to woo them, so suit is an old word for wooing.

clue.text: Hair tonic, perhaps, applied to promote growth

definitions.text: Hair tonic, perhaps, applied to promote growth

blocks.note: surface reading: lotion rubbed on the head to grow hair
setter's reading: manure or fertiliser spread on the surface of soil

explanation.surface: A lotion rubbed into the scalp in hope of growing hair.
explanation.walkthrough: A hair tonic is literally a dressing for the top of the head, but the gardening sense is fertiliser spread over the soil rather than dug in.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners spread compost or manure on the soil surface to feed plants, and that layer is called by this term.

clue.text: Bristling thug set on friar

indicators.note: set can mean arranged or put in order, so the letters are laid out afresh

blocks.note: Fra is the Italian title for a friar
the word itself, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tough sets upon a monk, who bristles with indignation.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, set on puts the rearranged thug after the friar.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraught with and bristling with are both said of something full of difficulty or danger.

clue.text: Prize Crossword in The 5 Gave cues to American investigator

blocks.note: surface padding: a page heading caught up with the clue in the scan, contributing nothing
first meaning: supplied an actor with lines, as a straight man does
second meaning: US slang for an FBI agent

explanation.walkthrough: The opening words are a stray heading from the newspaper page; the clue proper starts at Gave.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic's partner feeds him lines, and Americans call a federal agent of the FBI by this short slang word.

clue.text: A guru, otherwise a prophet

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: the two words supply all five letters

explanation.surface: A spiritual teacher who might alternatively be called a seer.
explanation.walkthrough: A guru and a prophet are near neighbours in meaning, which hides the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An augur was a Roman priest who foretold events from omens, so the word means a soothsayer or seer.

clue.text: One left after the soup, having mouth trouble

blocks.note: gumbo is a thick okra soup from Louisiana
the Roman numeral for one
the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A diner who stayed on after the soup course ends up with a sore mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: After places the one and left behind the soup, so they come last.
explanation.definitionFit: A gumboil is an abscess on the gum, a painful complaint inside the mouth.

clue.text: Today, perhaps, is my initiation into apple-polishing in US

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word could be something else if its letters were shuffled
an initiation is a beginning, so only the opening letter of the next word counts

blocks.note: the word to be rearranged
taken as written
the start of the word my

explanation.surface: Someone declares that today marks their first step into sucking up to the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Apple-polishing is American slang for currying favour, from the pupil who brings the teacher an apple.
explanation.definitionFit: Toadyism is fawning flattery of the powerful, exactly what Americans mean by apple-polishing.

clue.text: Putted softly, it somehow skipped along

indicators.note: somehow suggests an unspecified way of putting the letters together

blocks.note: taken as written
p, piano, is the musical mark for soft
taken as written

explanation.surface: A golfer taps the ball gently on the green and it hops along.
explanation.walkthrough: Softly looks like an adverb describing the putt, but it supplies the musical letter for quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To tittup is to move with a prancing, bouncing step, so a mincing skip along the ground.

clue.text: Stop one leaving the country

indicators.note: leaving means going away from, so that part drops out of the word

blocks.note: The Gambia is the small West African country
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A command to halt someone trying to emigrate.
explanation.walkthrough: Stop looks like a command, but it is the organ stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamba is an organ register with a string-like tone, named after the viola da gamba.

clue.text: Kind of frog - Tenniel's first character - did the high jump

indicators.note: the first character of a name is its opening letter

blocks.note: leapfrog, the game of vaulting over a crouching player
the start of the illustrator's name

explanation.surface: Tenniel's drawing of a frog character, perhaps from Alice, making a big jump.
explanation.walkthrough: John Tenniel illustrated Alice in Wonderland, which tempts a search for a frog character; only his initial is used.
explanation.definitionFit: To leap is to spring into the air, so the past tense matches a jump already made.

clue.text: Runs limited for these players

blocks.note: surface reading: cricketers or batsmen restricted in how many runs they score
setter's reading: a theatre company presenting each play for a short season

explanation.surface: A team of batsmen kept to a low score.
explanation.walkthrough: Runs and players suggest cricket, but the runs are theatrical seasons and the players are actors.
explanation.definitionFit: A repertory company stages several productions in rotation, each running only a short time.

clue.text: Farm cutter works as rough help

indicators.note: works suggests labouring at or processing material, reshaping the letters

blocks.note: all eleven letters of these three words

explanation.surface: An agricultural blade that is handy for heavy, rough labour.
explanation.definitionFit: The ploughshare is the cutting blade of a plough, which slices the soil on a farm.

clue.text: The hopeless imp masquerading as devilish character

indicators.note: masquerading means appearing in disguise, so the letters show up in a new form

blocks.note: every letter of the phrase

explanation.surface: A useless little demon dressing up as Satan's sidekick.
explanation.walkthrough: Imp is a natural partner for devilish, which disguises that the phrase is the raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: Mephistopheles is the demon to whom Faust sells his soul in the legend, a fiend of literature.

clue.text: Strict on school punishments here - bad luck!

blocks.note: a hard regime is a strict one
lines are sentences a pupil must copy out repeatedly as a penalty

explanation.surface: A sympathetic word to a pupil landed with a tough teacher's punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Hard lines is British slang said to commiserate, like tough luck; writing lines is a classic British school punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is an informal British expression of sympathy when someone suffers misfortune.

clue.text: Brittle container found in battery

blocks.note: first meaning: as an adjective, thin and fragile like china
second meaning: the casing of what hens lay in a battery farm

explanation.surface: A fragile casing inside an electrical cell.
explanation.walkthrough: Battery suggests electricity, but it is a battery of cages for laying hens.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes very thin, delicate porcelain or paint finish, and is literally the shell around a hen's egg.

clue.text: Getting a good grip with clubs used for close range work

definitions.note: describes what the answer is used for rather than naming it

blocks.note: grappling is seizing hold firmly
irons are golf clubs with metal heads

explanation.surface: A golfer gripping the clubs used for short approach shots.
explanation.walkthrough: Close range sounds like golf's short game, where irons are used, but it means boarding an enemy ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappling irons are hooked tools thrown to pull ships together for boarding, so they serve fighting at very short distance.

clue.text: Full series of deliveries completely finished

blocks.note: first meaning: in cricket, an over is a set of six balls, so a whole one
second meaning: entirely ended

explanation.surface: A courier has made every drop on the round and is done for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Deliveries sounds like post, but a delivery in cricket is a ball bowled, and six make an over.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is everyday English for something that has come to a final end, as when a match concludes.

clue.text: Egg, with a charge for salt

blocks.note: a nit is the egg of a louse
a rate is a price or fee

explanation.surface: An egg priced up for the salt to season it.
explanation.walkthrough: Egg suggests breakfast, but it is the louse's egg.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitrate is a chemical salt of nitric acid, such as saltpetre.

clue.text: Where Sabrina may have met a bore

definitions.text: Where Sabrina may have met a bore

blocks.clueFragment: Where Sabrina may have met a bore
blocks.note: surface reading: a woman stuck with a tedious companion at a party
setter's reading: a tidal wave surging up a river, in the waters of the river nymph

explanation.surface: Somewhere a woman called Sabrina got cornered by a tedious man.
explanation.walkthrough: Sabrina is the nymph of Britain's longest river in Milton's Comus, and that river is famous for its tidal bore, a wave that runs upstream.
explanation.definitionFit: The river flowing from Wales into the Bristol Channel is named Sabrina in Latin and has a celebrated tidal surge.

clue.text: What market gardeners are said to do in borders?

indicators.note: are said points to how the words sound when spoken rather than how they are written

blocks.note: growers who supply markets sell their vegetables

explanation.surface: A question about what vegetable growers do in their flower borders.
explanation.walkthrough: Veg is British slang for vegetables. Borders looks like part of the garden scene, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A selvedge is the woven edge of fabric that stops it fraying, so the plural means edges of cloth.

clue.text: Highly elusive, this taste of Rhine valley Riesling

indicators.note: a taste is a small sample, so only a sliver from inside the following words is taken

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the second and third words

explanation.surface: A rare sip of German wine from the Rhine valley.
explanation.walkthrough: Highly elusive, this works as a description: a nest set high on a crag is hard to reach.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is an eagle's nest built on a cliff or mountain top, high up and out of reach.

clue.text: Note on illuminated volume

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing placed on another follows it, so the musical note goes second

blocks.note: lit means lighted up
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A jotting about an illuminated manuscript book.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, the note on the illuminated part comes after it. Volume looks like a book, but it is a measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A litre is a metric unit of capacity, a measurement of liquid volume.

clue.text: Wriggler that could become a jelly fish?

definitions.text: Wriggler that could become a jelly fish?

blocks.note: surface reading: a jellyfish, the sea creature

blocks.clueFragment: Wriggler that could become a jelly fish?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a young creature that may grow up to be jellied, a London dish

explanation.surface: A wriggling larva that might grow into a jellyfish.
explanation.walkthrough: Jellied eels are a traditional London East End dish, so a young one could end up as a fish in jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: An elver is a young eel migrating upriver, a wriggling thing that grows into the adult.

clue.text: Rail signal accepts The Scotsman - maybe good idea!

indicators.note: to accept is to take something in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: BR was British Rail, the national railway
Ian is the stock Scottish man's name
a wave of the hand is a signal

explanation.surface: A railway signal system takes on a Scottish newspaper, perhaps a bright notion.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed, the Scotsman's name appears with its letters shuffled and no signal for it, a loose touch by the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainwave is a sudden clever thought or inspiration, so it may well be a good idea.

clue.text: The bark of a tree

blocks.note: first meaning: the deep howl of a hound
second meaning: the laurel whose leaves flavour cooking

explanation.walkthrough: Bark of a tree reads as the outer skin of a trunk; it is a dog's cry, and separately a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A hound's deep howling cry is called this, and the same word names the sweet laurel used in cooking.

clue.text: Nearly 100 involved in theft

indicators.note: involved means tangled up or intricate, so the letters are jumbled together

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Almost a hundred people mixed up in a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: Nearly looks like it qualifies the number, but it is raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is the legal term for stealing personal property, so it means theft.

clue.text: Oriental festival's name

blocks.note: Easter is the Christian spring festival
N is the standard abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: The name of a festival from the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental and the answer both describe things from the East, especially Asia.
